title: Paid every year, never recorded as competed
question: Which payees were paid in every fiscal year from 2019 to 2026 without a single payment recorded as competitively awarded?
finding: 2,110 payees were paid in all eight years and received $33.67 billion of the $44.69 billion of outside spending. 161 of them, paid $1 million or more ($6.43 billion together), have no payment recorded as competed. Most of that money sits under rules that do not say either way: construction contracts $4.50 billion; power for resale $446.4 million; property rent $353.0 million; management consulting services $334.4 million. Only 25 got most of their money under a rule that expressly sets competition aside, and 21 did so in every one of the eight years ($190.1 million), led by Epic State and Local Government LLC ($124.4 million, systems consulting services), Hyland Software Inc ($9.3 million, systems consulting services), R T Z Associates Inc ($6.5 million, systems consulting services). The departments that account for the 161: Public Utilities Commission $4.01 billion, Public Works $902.9 million, City Administrator $555.3 million, Public Health $346.2 million. Separately, 87 payees of any kind were paid under a no-competition rule in all eight years ($1.14 billion under those rules); the exceptions screens list them by contract.
how: Every payment line carries the purchasing rule staff keyed for it. A payee is listed when it was paid in each fiscal year 2019 to 2026 (a payment belongs to the year its voucher was issued in, read from the voucher number), received $1 million or more, and no line is keyed with a rule that says competed, bid or term contract. The columns split its money three ways: under a rule that sets competition aside (emergency, sole source, bidding waived by ordinance, other "not bid" wording); under a rule that does not say (for example "construction services", rent, agreements with public bodies); and with no rule keyed or a small purchase a department may make without bids. Ranked by the first of these, then by total.
limits: The rule is whatever staff keyed. "Construction services" does not say whether bids were taken, though the bid lists in the bid screens show that public works contracts are put out to bid; rent goes to whoever owns the building; electricity for resale is bought under its own rule. The list is where to look, not what was found. What would settle a row: the sole-source justification, or the bid tabulation the keyed rule fails to mention. "Construction services" is a purchasing label that does not record how the work was awarded, so this is a list of payees with nothing recorded as competed, not a list of work awarded without competition. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. The $992.6 million of outside spending that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier is in none of the figures here; it is used only to tell that a payee is not new.
